observations: Torah #125 contains one bechina relationship in the source text: נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה (good point) is בְּחִינַת חָסִיד (an aspect of a pious one). However, this yields only 2 nodes connected by 1 edge — far below the 3+ bechina-connected concepts threshold required for a new package proposal. The remaining concepts in the teaching (Tehillim, David HaMelekh, milchemet ha-yetzer hara, kaf zchut, Yehoshafat) are connected by eitza (practical advice / cause-and-effect) relationships, not bechina. The teaching is primarily practical guidance about how to say Tehillim — apply David's wars to one's own inner battle, and apply David's self-praise to finding one's own good points. These are causal/interpretive instructions, not shared-essence equivalences. The bechina pair (nekuda tova = chasid) is documented in the additions file for potential inclusion in the dataset, but does not warrant a new package on its own.
